correctness.rationale: The proof partitions all initial sets by the number of empty core-leaf pairs and handles every case. Two empty pairs permanently leave at least two white core neighbors; one empty pair without a black leaf has no first force; one empty pair with a black leaf clears by leaf-to-core, core-to-missing-core, then core-to-leaf forces; and no empty pair clears after leaf-only pairs activate their cores. The two successful regimes are disjoint and yield the polynomial directly. The standalone verifier independently checks every subset for \(2\le n\le8\), all coefficients, the minimum value, basis count, and total count.

value.rationale: The singleton-corona \(K_n\odot K_1\) is a canonical graph operation boundary that is explicitly outside the main order-at-least-two recurrence in the closest corona-product source. The result gives an exact structural rule for every initial set and, from it, the complete zero forcing polynomial, all minimum bases, and a closed total count. This is substantially more informative than recomputing a scalar zero forcing number and provides a natural benchmark for corona and whiskering questions.
